title: Seeing changes with diff
summary: git diff, git diff --staged and git diff HEAD compare different pairs of areas. Learn which is which and how to read a hunk.

steps.title: Three diffs, three questions
body: `git diff` always compares **two** things. Which two depends on the flags:
| `git diff` | What have I changed but **not staged**? |
| `git diff --staged` (same as `--cached`) | What **will** the next commit contain? |
| `git diff HEAD` | Everything changed since the last commit, staged or not |
> **Tip:** Run `git diff --staged` right before every commit. It is the commit you are about to make.

steps.prompt: You ran `git add .` and now `git diff` prints nothing. Does that mean you have no changes?
options: No: everything is staged, so the working tree matches the index. `git diff --staged` shows the changes
Yes: the working tree matches the last commit
No: `git diff` only works after the first commit
Yes: `git add` saved the changes, so there is nothing left to commit
steps.explain: Plain `git diff` compares working tree to index. After `git add .` those are equal, so it is empty even though the next commit is not.

items: An edit you saved but never added
A new file you just `git add`ed
The unstaged half of an `MM` file
A deletion you made with `git rm`
A deletion you made with plain `rm`
steps.explain: Untracked files never show in `git diff` at all: Git has nothing to compare them with until you add them.

steps.title: Reading a hunk
body: -    foreach (var i in items) sum += i.Price;
- `a/` is the old side, `b/` the new side.
- `@@ -10,4 +10,5 @@` is the **hunk header**: the old side starts at line 10 and spans 4 lines; the new side starts at line 10 and spans 5.
- A leading space is **context** (unchanged), `-` was removed, `+` was added.
Old count = context + removed lines. New count = context + added lines.

steps.prompt: A hunk has 3 context lines, 1 removed line and 2 added lines, starting at line 20 on both sides. What is its hunk header? (Write it exactly, like `@@ -A,B +C,D @@`.)
steps.explain: Old side: 3 context + 1 removed = 4 lines. New side: 3 context + 2 added = 5 lines.

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: show staged changes, list only the names of changed files, and show changes to one file since the last commit.
steps.explain: `--name-only` (or `--stat` for counts) gives a quick overview before reading the full diff. `--` separates revisions from file paths.

steps.prompt: Match the command to what it compares.
pairs: the tip of `main` vs the tip of `feature`

steps.prompt: Why does the diff mark a line as removed and re-added when you only changed its indentation?
options: Diff compares whole lines; any byte difference, including whitespace, makes it a different line
It is a bug in your editor
Git ignores whitespace, so this cannot happen
steps.explain: Use `git diff -w` to ignore whitespace while reviewing. And avoid mixing reformatting with real changes in one commit: reviewers cannot see the real change.

steps.title: Read the three diffs
prompt: In `~/shop` someone left a mix of staged and unstaged work. Use the diffs to sort it out:
1. Save the names of the files that are **staged** right now into `~/answers/staged.txt`, one per line (let Git print them).
2. `src/Config.cs` shows as changed, but nobody meant to change it. Prove that only whitespace changed (`git diff -w` prints nothing for it), then put it back to the committed version.
3. `src/Api.cs` was staged by mistake. Unstage it, but **keep** the edit in the working tree.
Leave `src/Cart.cs` as it is: its staged fix and its unstaged edit are both wanted.

checks.name: ~/answers/staged.txt lists the staged files
checks.fail: `~/answers/staged.txt` should list the files that were staged at the start. `git diff --staged --name-only` prints exactly that (run it before you unstage anything).

checks.name: src/Config.cs is back to the committed version
checks.fail: `src/Config.cs` still differs from the last commit. `git restore src/Config.cs` throws the working-tree change away.

checks.name: src/Api.cs is unstaged and still edited
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && git diff --cached --quiet -- src/Api.cs && grep -q 'GET /orders' src/Api.cs
checks.fail: `src/Api.cs` should be unstaged with its TODO line still in the file. `git restore --staged src/Api.cs` does that.

checks.name: src/Cart.cs keeps both changes
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && git diff --cached -- src/Cart.cs | grep -q 'Math.Round' && git diff -- src/Cart.cs | grep -q 'items.Count'
checks.fail: `src/Cart.cs` should still have the rounding fix staged and the `items.Count` edit unstaged. Press Reset scenario if it got mixed up.

hints: `git diff --staged --name-only` lists staged files. Redirect it: `> ~/answers/staged.txt` (make the folder first with `mkdir -p ~/answers`).
`git diff src/Config.cs` shows every line changed; `git diff -w src/Config.cs` (ignore whitespace) shows nothing. Then `git restore src/Config.cs`.
`git restore --staged src/Api.cs` moves it out of the index and leaves the file alone.
steps.explain: Three questions, three diffs: `git diff` (working tree vs index), `git diff --staged` (index vs last commit) and `git diff HEAD` (both together). `-w` hides whitespace-only changes, which is how you spot an editor that re-indented a file. `--name-only` and `--stat` give the overview before the detail.
